summary: Alfred Gell worked in other fields, earning degrees at Cambridge and LSE, where he studied under Edmund Leach. He held posts at the University of Sussex, Australian National University, London School of Economics, and was a British Academy Fellow.

Alfred Hillebrandt worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Breslau under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and at Munich under Martin Haug. He served as professor at the University of Breslau from 1883, becoming a full professor in 1887.
Alfred Körte worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics, having studied at the University of Bonn. His academic career included posts at Greifswald, Bonn, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and Leipzig.

Alfred Ludwig was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Vienna and Berlin under teachers including Albrecht Weber and August Boeckh. He completed his Habilitation at Vienna before holding professorships at Charles University from 1860.

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown was an academic who studied at King Edward's School and Cambridge. He held appointments at the University of Sydney, University of Chicago, University of Oxford, and the Fundação Escola de Sociologia e Política de São Paulo.

Ali S. Asani works in religious studies and Indology. After completing his studies at Harvard College and Harvard University, he served as a professor of Middle Eastern Studies and Indo-Muslim and Islamic Religion and Cultures at Harvard.

Alice Harris is a linguist who studied at Harvard University and the University of Massachusetts Amherst. She held academic posts at Vanderbilt University from 1979 to 2002 and at the University of Massachusetts Amherst.
Alice Y. Tseng specializes in Japanology and history and archaeology. She was a graduate student under Eugene Y. Wang and is attested as a professor at Boston University in 2013.

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under teachers including Saw Tun, Than Than Win, Carol S. Anderson, and doctoral supervisors Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins.

Alison Denton Jones works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Martin King Whyte as her doctoral supervisor, as well as under Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret H. Dornish.

Alka Patel works in history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at Mount Holyoke College and Harvard University, and served as Associate Professor at the University of California, Irvine.

Allan G. Grapard worked in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. from INALCO and held posts at the University of California, including ISF Professor of Shinto Studies and Professor Emeritus at UC Santa Barbara.

Allan Gibbard is a philosopher who studied at Swarthmore College and Harvard University. He held academic appointments at the University of Chicago, the University of Pittsburgh, and the University of Michigan from 1977 to 2016.
Allan H. Barr is a Sinologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Oxford in 1983. He held a post as Professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College.

Allen Wright Thrasher is an Indologist who completed doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and also studied under traditional teachers in India. He held a post at the Library of Congress from 1986 to 2014.
Allison Busch was an Indologist who studied under Sheldon Pollock. She served as Associate Professor of Hindi Literature at Columbia University.
Alnis Dickson works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed an MA at McGill University, where he studied under supervisor Lara Braitstein and teacher G. Victor Sōgen Hori.

Alois Anton Führer was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Julius Jolly and Georg Bühler. He served at St. Xavier's College, the State Museum in Lucknow, and as Archaeological Surveyor for the Archaeological Survey of India.
Alois Müller worked in linguistics and other fields. He held posts at Palacký University Olomouc, Vienna University Library, and served as Director of Graz University Library.

Aloysius Pieris specialized in religious and Buddhist studies, earning degrees from London, Sri Lanka, and Tilburg. He founded and directed the Tulana Research Centre and held chairs at Washington Theological Union, Union Theological Seminary, and Vanderbilt University.
